newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates NTT stg bond AAA,outlook negative.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates NTT stg bond AAA,outlook negative.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it assigned its AAA long-term rating to Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's (NTT) 250 million stg straight bond due December 2, 2003.
The rating outlook is negative, S&P said.
"The rating reflects NTT's dominant position and important role in the Japanese telecommunications market, and strong cash flow and financial profile among major international peers," S&P said.
Despite increased penetration by the new common carriers, NTT still maintains over 90 percent share of the domestic telephone market, S&P said.

NTT's consolidated operating income increased by 53.7 percent for the fiscal year ended March 31, 1996, as a result of increases in basic monthly charges and directory assistance services implemented in early 1995, and owing to continued growth of the Japanese cellular phone market, S&P said.
Although improving, profit levels are still lower than peak levels as a result of price competition with and loss of market share to the NCCs over the past several years, S&P said.

NTT's financial profile remains very strong. Funds from operations interest coverage is still over eight times, ranking among the highest of rated international peers. Strong internal cash flow covers a large portion of capital expenditures, which are high due to the cost of digitalising its network, S&P said. Consequently, there has been a marginal increase in debt usage, it said.
The final decision regarding the potential break-up of NTT into one long distance and two regional telephone companies is not expected until Spring 1997, S&P said.
A near-term rating action is not anticipated unless the Japanese government gives final approval for the break-up, or until sufficient details of the restructuring become available.
"Regardless of a potential break-up, heightening competition in the Japanese telecommunications industry could have adverse effects on NTT's dominant market position in the future," S&P said.
